sentences.text:
Ashamalla Yadamma, R.R.Dist., And Ano. vs Ravi Kumar,
Mahaboobnagar Dist., And ... on 13 December, 2023

Author: G. Radha Rani
Bench: G. Radha Rani
 The Honourable Dr. Justice G. Radha Rani
 M.A.C.M.A. No.5385 of 2008
Judgment:

This appeal is filed by the appellants - petitioners aggrieved by the award and decree dated 12.12.2005 passed in O.P. No.2468 of 2003 by the XIII Additional Chief Judge (FTC), City Civil Court, Hyderabad, seeking enhancement of compensation from Rs.2,65,500/- awarded by the Tribunal to Rs.3,00,000/- as claimed by them.

entities.text: XIII Additional Chief Judge (FTC), City Civil Court, Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The appellants-petitioners are the wife and son of the deceased Ashamalla Venkataiah.

The case of the petitioners in brief was that the deceased was working as a labour and was earning Rs.3,000/-
per month by the date of the accident on 12.06.2002.

On the said unfortunate date, while the deceased, along with one Kumar Goud, was travelling on a tractor/trailor bearing No. AP 22U 3726/3727 after loading fertilizers and were proceeding from Shadnagar to Ummenthala village and when reached near Gampa Cheruvu after crossing Mogiligidda on Parigi road at about 7.30 PM, the driver of the tractor/trailor drove the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner due to which the tractor/trailor turned turtle and the deceased Dr.GRR,J fell underneath the fertilizer bags and died on the spot.
The petitioners submitted that the Police Shadnagar registered a case vide Crime No.178 of 2002 for the offences under Sections 337 and 304-A IPC against the driver of the tractor/trailor.
The petitioners claimed compensation from the respondent Nos.1 and 2, owner and Insurer of the said vehicle.
3. The respondent No.1 remained exparte.
The respondent No.2 filed counter and called for strict proof of the petition averments.
The respondent No.2 further contended that the compensation claimed was excessive and exorbitant and prayed to dismiss the petition against them.
4. After framing the issues, the Tribunal caused enquiry in to the matter.
The petitioner No.1-wife of the deceased was examined as PW.1 and Exs.A1 to A5 were marked on behalf of the petitioners.
No oral evidence was adduced by the respondent No.2-Insurance company.

The copy of the policy was marked as Ex.B1.
5.
On considering the oral and documentary evidence on record, the Tribunal awarded an amount of Rs.2,65,500/- to the petitioners with interest at 6% per annum.

Dr.GRR,J Ashamalla Yadamma, R.R.Dist., And Ano. vs Ravi Kumar, Mahaboobnagar Dist., And ... on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78966657/
1 6.

entities.text: GRR,J Ashamalla Yadamma, R.R.Dist., And Ano. vs Ravi Kumar, Mahaboobnagar Dist
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal considered the age of the deceased as 38 years and his income as Rs.2,000/- per month i.e. Rs.24,000/- per annum and after deducting 1/3rd of the income towards his personal expenses and by applying the multiplier '16', calculated the loss of dependency as Rs.2,56,000/-.
The Tribunal awarded an amount of Rs.2,000/- towards funeral expenses, Rs.5,000/- towards loss of consortium and Rs.2,500/- towards loss of estate.

7. Aggrieved by the said award and decree, the petitioners preferred this appeal contending that as per the post mortem report, the age of the deceased was 35 years and hence, the Tribunal ought to have applied multiplier '17' as per the II Schedule of the Motor Vehicles Act and the income of the deceased ought to have been considered as Rs.36,000/- per annum.
The petitioner No.1 was entitled to Rs.16,000/- more on the count of consortium apart from statutory benefits.
8. Heard Sri T. Viswarupa Chary, learned counsel for the appellants-petitioners and Sri P. Harinath Gupta, learned counsel for respondent No.2-Insurance Company.
Dr.GRR,

J 9. The learned counsel for the appellants contended that though the appellants claimed the income of the deceased as Rs.3,000/- per month, the same could be considered as Rs.4,500/- per month as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Ramachandrappa v. The Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Limited 1.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. The Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Limited 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There was no bar on this Court to consider the monthly income of the deceased at more than the amount claimed and relied upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Laxmidhar Nayak v. Jugal Kishore Behera 2.

entities.text: Laxmidhar Nayak v. Jugal Kishore Behera 2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
He further contended that there is no restriction that compensation could be awarded only upto the amount claimed by the claimant and relied upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sanobanu Nazirbhai Mirza and others v.
Ahmedabad Municipal Transport Service 3 and the constitutional bench judgment of this Court in Adam Indur Muttemma v. Rathod Reddia 4.
10.

entities.text:
Sanobanu Nazirbhai Mirza and others v.
Ahmedabad Municipal Transport Service 3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Adam Indur Muttemma v. Rathod Reddia
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the respondent No.2-Insurance Company, on the other hand, contended that the award of the Tribunal was just and reasonable as the amount was awarded after considering all the aspects.
The accident occurred in the year 2002.

The amount (2011) 13 SCC 236 (2018) 1 SCC 746 (2013) 16 SCC 719 (2015 (4) ALD 585 (LB) Dr.GRR,J considered as income of the deceased at the rate of Rs.2,000/- per month at the relevant time of the accident was reasonable and there is no need to interfere with the award of the Tribunal
and prayed to dismiss the appeal.

11. As this appeal is filed challenging the quantum of compensation, this Court considers it not necessary to go into the other aspects like as to at whose negligence the accident occurred or on whom the liability arises.

12. With regard to quantum, the Tribunal considered the age of the deceased as 38 years via media as the appellants claimed the age of the deceased as 35 years and Ex.A4 post mortem report was also disclosing his age at 35 years, but the charge sheet and inquest report marked under Exs.A2 and A3 were disclosing the age of the deceased as 40 years.

2 13.

entities.text: Ashamalla Yadamma, R.R.Dist., And Ano. vs Ravi Kumar, Mahaboobnagar Dist
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
As the post mortem report marked under Ex.A4 is disclosing the age of the deceased as 35 years,
this Court considers that the same can be taken for assessing the compensation.
As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarla Verma v. Delhi Dr.GRR,J Transport Corporation 5, the relevant multiplier is '16' for the age group between 31 to 35 years.

entities.text: Sarla Verma v. Delhi Dr.GRR,J Transport Corporation 5
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As such, there is no change in the multiplier applied by the Tribunal.
The claimants claimed the earnings of the deceased as Rs.3,000/- per month.
But, the Tribunal considered the income of the deceased at Rs.2,000/- per month observing that as a rural labour, the deceased could not expect labour work daily.
The Hon'ble Apex Court in Ramachandrappa's case (1 supra) observed that:
"14. In the instant case, it is not in dispute that the appellant was aged about 35 years and was working as a Coolie and was earning `4500/- per month at the time of accident.
This claim is reduced by the Tribunal to a sum of `3000/- only on the assumption that wages of the labourer during the relevant period viz. in the year 2004, was `100/- per day.
This assumption in our view has no basis.
Before the Tribunal, though Insurance Company was served, it did not choose to appear before the Court nor did it repudiate the claim of the claimant.
Therefore, there was no reason for the Tribunal to have reduced the claim of the claimant and determined the monthly earning a sum of `3000/- per month.

Secondly, the appellant was working as a Coolie and therefore,
we cannot expect him to produce any documentary evidence to substantiate his claim.
In the absence of any other evidence contrary to the claim made by the claimant, in our view, in the facts of the present case, the Tribunal should have accepted the claim of the claimant.
We hasten to add that in all cases and in all circumstances, the Tribunal need not accept the claim of the claimant in the absence of supporting material.
It depends on the facts of each case.

In a given case, if the claim made is so exorbitant or if (2009) 6 SCC 121 Dr.GRR,J the claim made is contrary to ground realities, the Tribunal may not accept the claim and may proceed to determine the possible income by resorting to some guess work, which may include the ground realities prevailing at the relevant point of time.
In the present case, appellant was working as a Coolie and in and around the date of the accident, the wage of the labourer was between `100/- to 150/- per day or `4500/- per month.
In our view, the claim was honest and bonafide and, therefore, there was no reason for the Tribunal to have reduced the monthly earning of the appellant from `4500/- to `3000/- per month.

We,
therefore, accept his statement that his monthly earning was `4500/-."
14.
In the instant case also, we cannot expect the appellants- petitioners to produce any documentary evidence to prove the income of the deceased.

However, considering that the claim made by the appellants that the earnings of the deceased at Rs.3,000/- per month is honest and bonafide and the said claim is not exorbitant or contrary to the ground realities, the Tribunal ought to have accepted the same.
As such, it is considered fit to consider the earnings of the deceased at Rs.3,000/- per month.

However, considering the constitutional bench judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi 6 as future prospects are to be applied even in cases where the deceased was self employed and as the (2017) 16 SCC 680 Dr.GRR,J age of the deceased is considered as 35 years, 50% of his income is added towards future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
15. Hence, the income of the deceased is considered as Rs.3,000/- + Rs.1,500/- (50% of Rs.3,000/-)
= Rs.4,500/- per month.

As the dependents are two members, 1/3rd of the income is deducted towards personal expenses of the deceased and the loss of dependency can be calculated as Ashamalla Yadamma, R.R.Dist., And Ano. vs Ravi Kumar, Mahaboobnagar Dist., And ... on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78966657/

sentences.text: As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Magma General Insurance Company Limited v. Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram 7 , the appellant No.1-petitioner No.1 is entitled for spousal consortium while the appellant No.2-petitioner No.2 is entitled for parental consortium.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited v. Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram 7
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As such, an amount of Rs.40,000/- with 10% enhancement for every three years is to be awarded as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Pranay Sethi's case (5 supra) to both the appellants.

Hence,
the appellants are entitled to Rs.44,000/- each under this head.
An amount of Rs.15,000/- each with 10% increase for every three years is to be awarded towards loss of estate and funeral expenses.
As such, an amount of Rs.16,500/- each is awarded to the appellants under these conventional heads.

As such, the amount of compensation entitled by the appellants-petitioners under various heads is as follows:
1. Loss of dependency : Rs.5,76,000/-
2. Loss of consortium spousal consortium : Rs. 44,000/-
 parental consortium : Rs. 44,000/-
 3. Loss of estate : Rs. 16,500/-
 4. Funeral charges : Rs. 16,500/-
 -----------------
 Total : Rs.6,97,000/-
 ------------------
18.
The claim petition is filed for an amount of Rs.3,00,000/-.

But, as there is no restriction on this Court to award more than the amount claimed if it is considered just and reasonable, as per the judgments of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Nagappa v.
Gurudayal Singh 8, wherein it was held that:
"..... there is no restriction that compensation could be awarded only up to the amount claimed by the claimant.

In an appropriate case where from the (2003) 2 SCC 274 Dr.GRR,J evidence brought on record if Tribunal/court considers that claimant is entitled to get more compensation than claimed, the Tribunal may pass such award.
Only embargo is it should be 'just' compensation, that is to say, it should be neither arbitrary, fanciful nor unjustifiable from the evidence.
This would be clear by reference to the relevant provisions of the M.V. Act.

Section 166 provides that an application for compensation arising out of an accident involving the death of, or bodily injury to, persons arising out of the use of motor vehicles, or damages to any property of a third party so arising, or both, could be made (a) by the person who has Ashamalla Yadamma, R.R.Dist., And Ano. vs Ravi Kumar, Mahaboobnagar Dist., And ... on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78966657/
4 sustained the injury; or (b) by the owner of the property; or (c) where death has resulted from the accident, by all or any of the legal representatives of the deceased;
or (d) by any agent duly authorised by the person injured or all or any of the legal representatives of the deceased, as the case may be."
and of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sanobanu Nazirbhai Mirza's case (3 supra) as well as the constitutional bench judgment of this Court in Adam Indur Muttemma's case (4 supra) which also reiterates the same principle by referring to various judgments of the Hon'ble Apex Court and as it is a settled principle by now, it is considered fit to enhance the compensation amount from Rs.2,65,500/- as awarded by the Tribunal to Rs.6,97,000/-, which is considered as just and reasonable.
19.

sentences.text: In the result, the appeal is allowed enhancing the compensation from Rs.2,65,500/- as awarded by the Tribunal to Rs.6,97,000/- (Rupees six lakhs ninety seven thousand only) with Dr.GRR,J interest at 7.5% per annum on the enhanced amount.

The respondent No.2 - Insurance Company is directed to deposit the said amount within a period of two (02) months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment, after deducting the amount deposited, if any.
On such deposit, the appellants - petitioners are permitted to withdraw the entire amount in equal proportions, after payment of deficit court fee on the enhanced amount.
Miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
